c.tagline: A lakeside town of ancient churches on one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are cheap and metered but confirm the fare or that the meter is on before setting off; there is no Uber, so use ranks or phone a local taxi company.

emergency.note: 112 is the general European emergency number; it reaches police, fire and ambulance from any phone.

hood_landmark.Kaneo: Church of St John at Kaneo Ohrid
hood_landmark.Centar: Ohrid town centre Sveti Kliment square

avoid.reason: Agree taxi fares in advance and watch belongings on the crowded summer boardwalk; otherwise usual awareness.

hood_desc: The steep, cobbled UNESCO core rising from the lake through medieval churches, the ancient theatre and Samuel's Fortress; a maze of stone houses, konaks and viewpoints — the essential place to stay for sights and atmosphere.

The tranquil lakeside neighborhood below the Old Town, famous for the cliff-top Church of St John at Kaneo and its little swimming beach shaded by olive trees; serene and scenic, ideal for a romantic, restful stay.
The waterfront promenade of Kej strung with restaurants, cafes, bars and boat docks; the sociable, animated heart of the lakefront where the town comes out to stroll each evening.
The modern town center just back from the water around the main square and Sveti Kliment, with markets, shops, the bus station and everyday local life; the practical, convenient base.

The string of southern lakeshore resorts and beaches — Sveti Stefan, Lagadin and beyond toward the monastery of St Naum — lined with hotels and pebbly swimming coves; a quiet, holiday base on the water outside town.

water.note: Tap water is spring-fed and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Limited daytime service; buses are infrequent and stop running in the evening, so most visitors walk or take taxis.
transit.note: Ohrid has no metro or tram and only a sparse local bus service; the compact center is best walked, with cheap taxis and intercity buses (to Skopje, Bitola and Struga) filling the gaps.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash (denars) on board; there is no smart-card or app ticketing. Taxis are metered and inexpensive.

air: Ohrid St. Paul the Apostle Airport (OHD)
bus: Intercity coaches to Skopje (~3 hr), Bitola, Struga and Skopje International Airport
train: No railway serves Ohrid; the nearest rail is at Bitola and Kičevo

airport.name: Ohrid St. Paul the Apostle Airport (OHD)

transit.m: Taxi to Ohrid centre (~15 min) — the main option, as there is no scheduled airport bus

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving about 10% at restaurants is customary for good service.
